questions.q: What does ADF Desktop Integration (ADFdi) actually do?
options: It zips CSV files and uploads them to UCM
It extends Oracle's application framework into Microsoft Excel, letting a live Fusion page talk directly to a connected spreadsheet
It is a reporting tool unrelated to data entry
It replaces the need for Oracle Fusion entirely
questions.explain: ADFdi connects Excel directly to a live Fusion page, letting users download, edit, and upload data with the same validation the web page applies.

questions.q: How does ADFdi's structure differ from the FBDI pipeline covered in earlier chapters?
options: ADFdi skips the ZIP/UCM upload and the separate load-then-import steps — the spreadsheet talks to the application directly, with no staging layer
They are identical in every respect
ADFdi requires an even longer pipeline than FBDI
ADFdi only works for Fixed Assets
questions.explain: FBDI relies on templates, ZIP files, UCM, and two separate scheduled processes with interface-table staging. ADFdi bypasses nearly all of that, connecting directly to the live application.

questions.q: Where do you go to download the Excel add-in that ADFdi depends on?
options: The File Import and Export page
The Scheduled Processes work area
A third-party app store
Download Desktop Integration, found under Tools in the Fusion navigator
questions.explain: Download Desktop Integration, under Tools, provides the installer (commonly an MSI file) that adds the ADFdi ribbon and connectivity to Excel.

questions.q: Why does ADFdi require macros to be enabled in Excel, similar to a problem covered in Chapter 2?
options: Because Excel cannot open any file without macros enabled
Because macros have nothing to do with ADFdi at all
Because ADFdi's upload and validation logic runs through macros, the same root cause as the CSV-generation macro used by FBDI templates
Because macros are required only for printing
questions.explain: Just like the FBDI template's CSV-generation macro, ADFdi's core functionality depends on macros being allowed to run in Excel.

questions.q: What symptom typically appears if an ADFdi prerequisite (like the installed add-in or enabled macros) is missing, rather than a clear error message?
options: Oracle Fusion automatically installs the missing component
A missing ribbon, a grayed-out action, or an upload that silently does nothing
The entire Oracle Fusion environment becomes permanently unavailable
A loud pop-up error appears immediately every time
questions.explain: Missing prerequisites tend to produce quiet, confusing symptoms — like a missing ribbon or a silent failed upload — rather than an obvious, clear error message.
